author: Mark Atwood
text: Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — 7 idiomatic-rust findings filed (.29-.35). No P0/P1 idiom defects. The Rust idiom posture is competent: forbid(unsafe_code), no panics in library code outside test_support, proper use of #[non_exhaustive] on most public types (one miss already flagged by JMAP-ayoz.24), consistent use of Result + ? propagation, idiomatic let-else for early-return guards, idiomatic match/if-let chains. The findings are mostly clippy-tier polish (.29, .30, .33, .34, .35) plus two structural items: .31 (DRY between get_changes and get_metadata_changes inside the same file) and .32 (HashMap-allocation pattern that propagates across the canonical-cookie-cut family). One finding (.35) was reclassified mid-pass: the State::from(.to_string().as_str()) pattern is workspace-wide across 5 cookie-cut siblings, not a metadata-server-specific divergence — the comment on .35 documents the cross-sibling scope and tags this as a propagation regression where the canonical (mail-server) is already correct.
